notes: Background: mid-market product analytics SaaS; heavy real-time instrumentation and in-app help widget used by customer success teams.
Initial interest: started on Hosted API for fast integration (dec 2025) to prototype contextual help and reranking of search results.

POC results summary: hosted API met quality bar for reranking and KB retrieval; typical chat reply p50 ~60ms server-side, p95 ~125ms for 512-token prompts; embedding recall + rerank improved CTR by estimated 12% in pilot cohort.

Why Dedicated: predictable throughput for peak usage windows, data isolation/VPC requirement for enterprise customers, and unit cost reduction at scale (they project 3-4x cost improvement vs hosted with a Dedicated commit).

Commercial ask (customer): prefers a stepped ramp (3-month ramp) with a lower initial monthly commit and predictable monthly increases; requests baseline burst allowance of 25% of commit for free and capped overage pricing after that.

Redwood proposal (draft): 12-month Dedicated contract, initial commit equivalent to 4 A100 GPUs (baseline), 30% optional burst credit built into month 1-3 ramp, overage priced at negotiated per-second / per-token rate; option to add extra GPUs during high season with 72-hour notice.

Negotiation points in flight: customer wants explicit ramp schedule in SOW (month-by-month commit targets), finance wants an annualized discount tier tied to commit increase, legal requests explicit data residency language for EU customers.

Quote specifics being debated: customer asked for lower effective per-token rate if they commit to 6-month minimum (we counter with 12-month term + modest uplift). Estimated ARR range on table 150k-350k depending on commit tier chosen.

Technical/ops notes: SE conducted stress test (Mar 3 meeting ff_2026-03-03_1102) simulating 1.2x peak concurrency; observed KV cache hit-rate benefits reduce token churn by ~18% which affects cost modeling.
